source1: Svat Soucek, The Shaybanids, ch. 11 in A History of Inner Asia, Cambridge University Press, 2000 - https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/abs/history-of-inner-asia/shaybanids/681328EFAC754EF2B9D3E7CF4BFE8CB7
notes: Soucek: both Timurids and Shaybanids were Sunni Muslims, giving fundamental continuity. Shaybani took Samarkand 1500-01 and Herat 1507; Britannica notes he was an accomplished poet and the dynasty built madrasas and mosques.

Mu'izz al-Dawla entered Baghdad Dec 945. Buyids were Daylamite Shi'ite Muslims ruling under Sunni Abbasid caliphs (same tradition, different branch); Iranica notes coins inscribed shahanshah, showing written administration.

source1: Inna N. Medvedskaya and Muhammad A. Dandamayev, Media, Encyclopaedia Iranica, 2006 - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/media
notes: Coded the Medes. Iranica: Mazdaism with Indo-Iranian traditions, Magi priests; no Mesopotamian cult adoption (Medes plundered Ehulhul, Harran); unknown whether Medes had writing. Babylonian coalition partner shared Mesopotamian tradition.

notes: French elite of Catholic heritage, but the Directory resumed an assault on Catholic worship after Fructidor 1797. Venice passed to Catholic Habsburg Austria under Campo Formio (Oct 1797), ending its independence; same tradition by inference.

Muslim Ifat became tributary after Amda Seyon's 1328 victory and was destroyed by Yeshaq I in 1415. Christian Solomonic emperors fought Muslim states and remained Christian; earliest Ethiopian chronicle covers Amda Seyon's reign.

source1: Yonatan Binyam, The Conflicts between Christian Aksum and Jewish Himyar in Pre-Islamic Arabia, CORE Coproduced Religions (Universitat Bern / IAS Princeton), 2023 - https://coproduced-religions.org/resources/case-studies/the-conflicts-between-christian-aksum-and-jewish-himyar-in-pre-islamic-arabia
